# Trial specs

## fieldwork activities

|  |  |
|:---------------:|-------------------------------------------------------|
| **4/14** | Planted swath of experiment to MN Rothsay Spring Wheat. Truax planter and 5725? wheat tractor with gps. Seeded \~1.5 inches deep. |
| **4/15** | baseline soil samples collected by block. Starting plots on southernmost tire track. 4 pushes 0-6" for 0-6inch , 2 pushes for 6-24", by block. |
| **4/15** | Fertilized appropriate plots with pre weighed baggies of anvil treated urea and ammonium sulfate. |
| **4/30** | cultivated the northern and southern edge, potentially shrinking the harvest length of the northern and southern ranges/blocks |
| **5/19** | applied fertilizer at prescribed rates. Also flagged out field |
| **5/23** | ndvi measurements: 0.02 variance of ndvi in same plot. So plot 101 at 6877 could be remeasured at 7077 or 6677. Walked middle of the 8 ft plot, 15 ft length. Biomass sampling: 1 meter of row collected in middle of the plot at the base, placed in bag. Some plots done by kahlid were 3 rows at 1 meter instead of 1 row at 1 meter, we will figure out which plots by using weight of bags, then we will need to account for this at grain harvest as well. |
| **5/23** | sprayed 27 fl oz of wolverine on wheat (second application due to first one not being successful. Hoping for control of some grasses |
| **6/24** | Soil sampled every plot. 4 pokes 0-6 inches. 2 pokes 6-24. |
| **7/24** | staging check |
| **7/28** | started combining alleys. 1/4 completed, but settings mostly dialed in |
| **7/30** | combine harvest- |
| **8/6** | soil samples. 3 push 0-6", 1 push 6-24". |

## NDVI

```{r}
#| label: fig-ndvi
#| fig-cap: "NDVI across two sampling dates. Green box indicates mean within sampling date. Treatments are ordered where 150N-20S is highest mean NDVI across both dates and 50N-10S is lowest mean NDVI when averaged across both dates."

dat %>% 
  select(date, plots, block, treatment, ndvi) %>% 
  drop_na(ndvi) %>% 
  mutate(treatment = fct_reorder(treatment,ndvi,
                                 .fun = mean)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(treatment,ndvi)) +
  geom_point() +
  stat_summary(
    geom = "point",
    fun = mean,
    col = 3,
    size = 2,
    shape = 15,
    stroke = 2
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~date, 
             scales = "free") +
  labs(x="")
```

# Grain (methods comparison)

Combine uses a harvest master system for plot yields, moisture and test weight

This was compared against a Perten 5200 moisture and test weight analyzer along with weighing the entire plot weight (bagged in the cab) on a scale after storing in a dryer for a couple days

## kg ha

```{r}
#| label: fig-yieldkgha
#| fig-cap: "Grain yield in kilograms per hectare between the combine weight system vs the entire sample being brought back to lab and weighed. Note when weighed by hand the sample was dryer so this explains lower weights. Outlier removed."
dat %>% 
  filter(grain_kgha_byhand<7000) %>% 
  select(date, plots, block, treatment,
         grain_kgha_harvestMaster,
         grain_kgha_byhand) %>% 
  drop_na(grain_kgha_harvestMaster, grain_kgha_byhand) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(grain_kgha_harvestMaster, grain_kgha_byhand),
    names_to = "method",
    values_to = "yield"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         grain_kgha_harvestMaster = "Combine",
                         grain_kgha_byhand = "By Hand")) %>% 
  mutate(treatment = fct_reorder(treatment, yield, .fun = mean)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = yield, color = method, shape = method)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 3, alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(color = method, shape = method),
    geom = "point",
    fun = mean,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "",
       y = "Yield (kg/ha)",
       color = "Method",
       shape = "Method")
```

-   lower N treatments tended to yield higher. Lodging?

\newpage

## lodging

```{r}
#| label: fig-yieldkghalodging
#| fig-cap: "Grain yield estimation from combine with lodging scores where 1 = no lodging and 9 = flat on the ground."

dat %>%
  filter(grain_kgha_harvestMaster < 7000, grain_kgha_byhand < 7000) %>%
  select(treatment, grain_kgha_harvestMaster, grain_kgha_byhand, lodging_score_atharvest) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(grain_kgha_harvestMaster, grain_kgha_byhand),
    names_to = "method",
    values_to = "yield"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    method = recode(method,
                    grain_kgha_harvestMaster = "Combine",
                    grain_kgha_byhand = "By Hand"),
    treatment = fct_reorder(treatment, yield, .fun = mean)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = yield, color = lodging_score_atharvest, shape = method)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7, position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", direction = -1, name = "Lodging Score\nFrom Combine") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Combine" = 17, "By Hand" = 16)) +  # triangle for Combine, circle for By Hand
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Yield (kg/ha)",
    shape = "Method"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```

-   low yields driven by lodging

## test weight

```{r}
#| label: fig-testweight
#| fig-cap: "Grain test weight values were reasonable using  using the Perten 5200 (i.e. By Hand) and were mostly mirrored by on board test weight estimator on combine, but those values will require a correction"


# Calculate mean test weight by treatment for By Hand
byhand_order <- dat %>%
  drop_na(grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor) %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  summarize(mean_byhand = mean(grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(mean_byhand) %>%
  pull(treatment)

dat %>% 
  filter(grain_kgha_byhand < 7000) %>% 
  select(date, plots, block, treatment,
         grain_testweight_lbbu_harvestMaster,
         grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor) %>% 
  drop_na(grain_testweight_lbbu_harvestMaster, grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(grain_testweight_lbbu_harvestMaster, grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor),
    names_to = "method",
    values_to = "test weight"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         grain_testweight_lbbu_harvestMaster = "Combine",
                         grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor = "By Hand")) %>%
  # Reorder factor using By Hand order
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = byhand_order)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = `test weight`, color = method, shape = method)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 3, alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(color = method, shape = method),
    geom = "point",
    fun = mean,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~method, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "",
       y = "Test weight estimation (lb/bu)",
       color = "Method",
       shape = "Method")

```

-   lower N treatments tended to have higher test weights.

## bu acre

```{r}
#| label: fig-buacre
#| fig-cap: "Grain yield in bushels per acre using only the by hand method because the test weight data was unreliable from the combine."


# Step 1: Compute treatment order based on By Hand yield (kg/ha)
byhand_order <- dat %>%
  filter(grain_kgha_byhand < 7000) %>%
  drop_na(grain_kgha_byhand) %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  summarize(mean_byhand = mean(grain_kgha_byhand, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(mean_byhand) %>%
  pull(treatment)

# Step 2: Main plot with corrected bu/acre
dat %>% 
  # glimpse()
  filter(grain_kgha_byhand < 7000) %>% 
  select(date, plots, block, treatment,
         grain_kgha_harvestMaster,
         grain_kgha_byhand,
         grain_testweight_lbbu_harvestMaster,
         grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor) %>% 
  drop_na(grain_kgha_harvestMaster, grain_kgha_byhand,
          grain_testweight_lbbu_harvestMaster,
          grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor) %>% 
  # Convert kg/ha → lb/acre → bu/acre
  mutate(
    lb_acre_byhand = grain_kgha_byhand * 2.20462 / 2.47105,
    lb_acre_harvestMaster = grain_kgha_harvestMaster * 2.20462 / 2.47105,
    bu_acre_byhand = lb_acre_byhand / grain_testweight_lbbu_byhand_grainsensor,
    bu_acre_harvestMaster = lb_acre_harvestMaster / grain_testweight_lbbu_harvestMaster
  ) %>% 
  # Pivot longer for plotting
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(bu_acre_harvestMaster, bu_acre_byhand),
    names_to = "method",
    values_to = "bu_acre"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         bu_acre_harvestMaster = "Combine",
                         bu_acre_byhand = "By Hand"),
         # Reorder treatments using By Hand order
         treatment = factor(treatment, levels = byhand_order)) %>% 
  filter(method=="By Hand") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = bu_acre, color = method, shape = method)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 3, alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(color = method, shape = method),
    geom = "point",
    fun = mean,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "",
       y = "Yield (bu/acre)",
       color = "Method",
       shape = "Method")


```

-   high N treatments tended to do worse

## moisture content

```{r}
#| label: fig-moisturecontent
#| fig-cap: "Moisture content at harvest (combine) and after dryer (By Hand)."

# Step 1: Compute treatment order based on Combine moisture
combine_order <- dat %>%
  filter(grain_kgha_byhand < 7000) %>%
  drop_na(grain_moisturepercent_harvestMaster) %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  summarize(mean_combine_moisture = mean(grain_moisturepercent_harvestMaster, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(mean_combine_moisture) %>%  # ascending order
  pull(treatment)


# Step 2: Main plot for grain moisture
dat %>% 
  filter(grain_kgha_byhand < 7000) %>% 
  select(date, plots, block, treatment,
         grain_moisturepercent_harvestMaster,
         grain_moisturepercent_byhand_grainsensor) %>% 
  drop_na(grain_moisturepercent_harvestMaster,
          grain_moisturepercent_byhand_grainsensor) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(grain_moisturepercent_harvestMaster,
             grain_moisturepercent_byhand_grainsensor),
    names_to = "method",
    values_to = "moisture_percent"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         grain_moisturepercent_harvestMaster = "Combine",
                         grain_moisturepercent_byhand_grainsensor = "By Hand"),
         # Reorder treatments using Combine moisture order
         treatment = factor(treatment, levels = combine_order)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = moisture_percent, color = method, shape = method)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 3, alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(color = method, shape = method),
    geom = "point",
    fun = mean,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "",
       y = "Grain moisture (%)",
       color = "Method",
       shape = "Method")

```

-   Higher N treatments had higher moisture at harvest

-   All were dried down from 12-15% moisture at harvest to around 10% before the "by hand" weighing, test weight and moisture determination on the Perten 5200

# Discussion

## Can we trust the combine?

### Moisture

Probably. I think 13% moisture at harvest is reasonable, but didn't do a thorough comparison.

### Test weight

No. Setting was set incorreclty. Combine trended simlar to Perten 5200, but not exactly. That's why it was nice to have the backup of the benchtop Perten 5200

### Plot yield

Probably. Didn't compare with quadrat harvest, but compared with taking the entire sample and weighing in the lab vs just taking a subsample we should be relativley confident we'll capture treatment differences.

## Lessons learned

Our lab is well suited to do trials like this. Plant all 1 variety. Multiple soil samples by plot. Tissue sampling. Combine harvest. We could easily become a site in other researchers trials and generate pretty good data and take good notes and photos and perform good QAQC on the data.

NDVI and biomass harvest data were too variable to be very useful in this trial.

Drone photos are incredibly valuable for verifying information like lodging and crop condition.
